mechanism_narrative: Persistent negative RETAIL_REC trend (declining from -8.7% to -12.3% over four weeks) reflects an entrenched contraction in discretionary mobility. This downward momentum continues into the next four weeks, producing further retail-and-recreation decline relative to the baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, or reverses to positive territory.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM mobility (sustained 9–12% above baseline) indicates essential-goods shopping remains robust. This substitution effect crowds out discretionary retail visits; consumers prioritize necessity over recreation, suppressing RETAIL_REC further over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 9% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable at 9.3–11.9% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its t-0w level within the next 14 days, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 5% while RETAIL_REC remains negative.

mechanism_narrative: Severe TRANSIT contraction (−17.7% to −22.3%) blocks commute-based retail access. When transit mobility falls below −20%, retail footfall cannot recover because consumers lack the mobility infrastructure to reach shopping districts. This threshold-driven mechanism suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below −20% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at −21.6%, −19.3%, −22.3% in weeks t-2w, t-1w, t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers to above −15% within the next 28 days and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above its t-0w level.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between depressed WORKPLACES (−12.1% at t-0w) and elevated RESIDENTIAL (4.0%) signals a shift to remote work and home-based activity. This dual regime suppresses commute-linked retail visits and redirects discretionary spending to online channels, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES below −12% AND RESIDENTIAL above 3.5% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at −12.1% and RESIDENTIAL at 4.0% at t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above −5% or RESIDENTIAL falls below 2% while RETAIL_REC remains below −10%.

mechanism_narrative: Negative PARKS mobility (−8.0% at t-0w, down from +20.3% at t-3w) signals a seasonal or weather-driven shift away from outdoor activity. This contraction in outdoor recreation crowds consumers indoors toward retail-and-recreation venues, producing a modest recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0% after sustained positive levels
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from +20.3% to −8.0% over four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS remains negative and RETAIL_REC continues to decline in week t+1w, or PARKS rebounds above +5% without RETAIL_REC rising.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between sustained TRANSIT suppression (−22.3% at t-0w) and declining WORKPLACES (−12.1%) indicates policy-driven mobility restrictions. Under this regime, retail recovery is blocked by both supply-side (worker absence) and demand-side (consumer access) constraints. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below −20% AND WORKPLACES below −10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:Both series negative and stable across four weeks
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES recovers to baseline (0%) within 28 days and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above −5%.

mechanism_narrative: Stabilization of RETAIL_REC at −12.3% (minimal week-on-week change from t-1w to t-0w) indicates the contraction has reached a floor. Absent further shocks to TRANSIT or WORKPLACES, RETAIL_REC will stabilize or recover modestly over the next two weeks as consumers adjust to the new equilibrium.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC change between t-1w and t-0w is less than 1 percentage point in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC at −11.3% (t-1w) and −12.3% (t-0w), a change of −1.0 pp
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls below −15% within the next 14 days, or TRANSIT/WORKPLACES deteriorate by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained positive GROCERY_PHARM (9–12%) combined with negative PARKS (−8.0%) indicates consumers are redirecting mobility toward essential and indoor activities, away from outdoor recreation. This behavioral shift will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next one week as discretionary retail remains crowded out by necessity-driven and indoor-focused mobility.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above 9% AND PARKS below 0% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 10.9% and PARKS at −8.0% at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS recovers to above +5% while GROCERY_PHARM falls below 8%, or RETAIL_REC rises above −10% within seven days.
